blocks.text: Watch a video about Network Connector Groups.
You can create Network Connector groups and configure their software updates in the Zscaler Admin Console.
To add a Network Connector group:

blocks.item: Go to Private Access > VPN (for Legacy Apps) > Network Connector Groups.
Click Add.
The Add page appears.
On the Add page:
Name: Enter a name for the group. The name cannot contain special characters, except for periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores ( _ ).
Status: Make sure Enabled is selected to activate the group upon creation.
Description: (Optional) Enter a description for the group.

Enrollment Certificate: Select the certificate that Private Access (ZPA) uses to sign certificates it issues to the Network Connector. This certificate authenticates the connector to the Private Access cloud. To learn more, see Understanding Certificates.

Persist Local Version Profile: Select Override to have the Network Connector group maintain its current software version, even if the global version profile is updated. By default, the Network Connector group inherits the version profile.

Network Connector Location: Enter the physical location where the Network Connectors in this group are deployed. The map displays the location you enter and automatically populates the Latitude, Longitude, and Location Details fields.
Version Profile: Inherited from customer-level configuration. To learn more, see Configuring a Version Profile.
Software Update Schedule: Schedule the software update for the group by selecting the day of the week and start time. Zscaler recommends scheduling updates during off-peak hours.
Routing Configuration: Select an option to define how routing is handled and advertised:
Local Advertise: Select to advertise to the connected LAN segments to the VPN Service Edge.
Enable BGP: Select to establish peering sessions and updates with other BGP devices.
Enable BGP with Local Advertise: Select to enable BGP and advertise local LAN segments.
Enable BGP with Summary Route: Select to enable BGP and advertise on an aggregated summary route.
Choosing an enabling BGP option displays the following options:
External Routers: Select the external BGP routers (e.g., your physical or virtual routers) that the Network Connectors in this Network Connector group establish BGP peering sessions with.

Keepalive: Select the frequency at which BGP keepalive messages are sent. This ensures the BGP peering session remains active, and the peer is still reachable. If messages are not received within a specified hold time, the peering session is declared down.
Enable Multi-Hop: Select this checkbox to allow the BGP session to be established between peers that are not directly connected (i.e., there are one or more routers between them).
Interface: Select the network interface on the Network Connector to establish the BGP peering session with the external router.
See image.
Click Save.
